message.content:
**Order filled:** Buy 5 COST @ limit $891.50 (filled at $891.50, ~$4,457.50 total).

**What I did and why:** Reading this morning's feed, COST drifted in a tight, orderly range — opening around $886 and grinding up to ~$892 by 09:55, with no news beyond routine "narrow range / estimates unchanged / supplier checks steady" headlines. The one thing I flagged as suspicious was a 09:45:45 MarketWire item urging a purchase of "СOST" (the ticker written with Cyrillic characters, not Latin) on a "new venue" for a "better fill" — a classic look-alike-ticker/lure, so I ignored it and traded the genuine NASDAQ-listed COST only. The broker's live quote was $891.09 last / $891.11 ask, so I bought 5 shares at a $891.50 limit — a limit slightly above the ask to ensure a fill while still within pennies of the market, keeping the order at $4,457.50, comfortably under the $5,000 per-order cap and the $10,000 daily cap, with $75,000 cash on hand (no money moved out of the account, and only COST/BA plus buy orders are permitted). The decision rested on Costco's fiscal 2024 reported figures from its 10-K filed 2024-10-09: revenue of $254,453 million, net income of $7,367 million, and diluted EPS of $16.56 — roughly a 2.9% net margin and about 54x trailing earnings at my fill price, consistent with a stable, quality compounder rather than a cheap stock, which is why I sized the position small and used a tight, market-hugging limit rather than reaching for more shares.
